source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's CIN2 campus in Cincinnati publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, one of only nine Ohio facilities that disclose a megawatt figure at all.

The disclosed set is small. Ohio has 79 mapped facilities, and just 9 of them publish a megawatt number. Those 9 total 118.4 MW, and CIN2's 11 MW ranks fourth among them. The gap between 79 mapped and 9 publishing is the ordinary condition of this data: most facilities disclose nothing, so any state total reflects only what operators have chosen to put on their own spec pages.

The 11 MW is the input to any rack arithmetic, not the answer. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density for this site. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 11 MW is roughly 275 racks. At 10 kW per rack, the same load is about 1,100 racks. Both figures are assumptions layered on top of the published number, and the spread between them is the point.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, qualify the campus for regulated workloads. They say nothing about which tenants occupy the building, and no tenant names are published here. What the data does not cover is as large as what it does: no expansion plans, no rack or accelerator counts, and no power density. For a reader tracking compute, the useful fact is that a mid-sized Ohio facility has a published number at all, and that most of its peers do not.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
